newsitem.title: UK: UK SFA fines Fidelity Brokerage,lifts restrictions.
newsitem.headline: UK SFA fines Fidelity Brokerage,lifts restrictions.

text.p: British financial regulator the Securities and Futures Authority on Thursday fined Fidelity Brokerage Services, the British retail stockbroking arm of Fidelity Investments, 200,000 pounds for rule breaches.

Fidelity, which admitted failings in its settlements system, also agreed to pay costs of 162,500 pounds, the SFA said in a statement, adding it had lifted restrictions on Fidelity's business, which have been in place since last October.

The SFA said Fidelity had experienced serious operational difficulties as a result of converting to a new computer system and an increased volume of business. This led to accounting and reconciliation problems and numerous customer complaints.

"SFA...is satisfied that the firm now has adequate systems and controls in place to enable it to take on new customers and to introduce new services and...has restored a satisfactory level of customer service," the SFA said,
But SFA spokesman David Jones told Reuters the watchdog would "keep close tabs on how they are resuming that business" and Fidelity would be providing regular reports on its progress.

In reaching the settlement, SFA said it had taken into account the fact that investors' money and securities had not been in danger, Fidelity had co-operated fully with it and the firm had "suffered a significant loss of revenue as a result of the restrictions on new business".
Fidelity had also taken appropriate measures to compensate customers and had devoted significant resources to remedying operational problems and addressing customer concerns.
